markers.reading: The narrated Mawar downtime runs from the winter of 1747–48 through spring 1749, before the new adventure.

evidence.quote: it was November of 1747.
the winter is bitterly cold and storm-lashed
It's not till May of that year that the winter… that the weather finally breaks.
The fall of 1748 lingers
Spring arrived—of 1749
It is now May 26, 1749.
past 18 months

markers.note: The start is month-level, not an invented November day; distant historical news does not extend the interval.

markers.reading: The new Hamri adventure opens on May 26, 1749; the meeting is first called evening and later corrected to late afternoon.

evidence.quote: It is now May 26, 1749.
in the evening of a pleasantly warm spring day
On a pleasant evening
it's dinner time, but you send a… or late afternoon, I guess

time.basis: Explicit spoken date; later DM correction of the same continuing meeting from evening/dinner time to late afternoon.

markers.reading: Yazran arrives about half an hour after the messenger is sent.

evidence.quote: And about half an hour later, he shows up, his name is Yazran.

duration.basis: Explicit elapsed wait for the priest

markers.reading: A further few minutes pass waiting for Ovina, approaching dinner time.

evidence.quote: A few more minutes pass. Another few minutes, another few minutes. Approaching dinner time now.

duration.basis: Explicit elapsed wait, without a numerical total

markers.reading: It is now night as the party settles on departing in the morning.

evidence.quote: it's now night, so probably best to just go in the morning

markers.reading: The next morning dawns after the night in Hamri: May 27 by the spoken opening date and explicit next-morning transition.

evidence.quote: So the next morning dawns… bright and warm.

time.basis: Next morning after the independently spoken May 26 date, not YAML-derived

markers.reading: The boat leaves around 07:38 and reaches the North Cliffs area after about an hour, on the dropping tide.

evidence.quote: you leave at, you know, 7.38 in the morning
It takes you an hour or so to get out to this area of the cliff

start.basis: DM says 7.38 in the morning with conversational qualification

end.basis: Inferred from the stated approximate departure and hour of actual sailing

duration.basis: Repeated actual sailing duration; earlier one-to-two-hour forecast is not separately counted

markers.reading: Ryu takes the offered ten-minute Beast Sense ritual before scouting through Turk’s senses.

evidence.quote: you can cast it as a ritual by just taking 10 minutes to prepare
Let's do it.
Turk, carrying Ryu's… senses… dives underwater

duration.basis: Accepted ritual followed by its resolved sensory scouting

markers.reading: Over the next few minutes the party finishes the last two water creatures.

evidence.quote: In the next few minutes, you manage to… kill all these last two creatures

duration.basis: Explicit compressed cleanup after the marid falls

markers.reading: The party returns to the Leviathan Inn that afternoon, May 27; Rayna’s extra night and next-morning departure remain future plans.

evidence.quote: That afternoon, you return to the Leviathan Inn

time.basis: Same day as the explicitly narrated next morning after May 26

yamlCheck.dateAnchor: YAML drStart/drEnd are null. The transcript independently says May 26, 1749, followed by the next morning and that afternoon (May 27). Earlier narrated downtime starts in winter 1747–48 with only a month-level November reference.
yamlCheck.explanation: No YAML dates exist to match or contradict. One explicit overnight is established in the focused adventure; the approximately 18-month downtime has no exact opening day, so a total span cannot be counted. Rayna’s planned additional night and departure are not completed play.
